question: Which of the following statements are correct? 1. The seventh boss defeated by the player in Chapter 5 is Flint Commander 2. The seventh boss defeated by the player in Chapter 3 is Green-backed Dragon 3. The fifth boss defeated by the player in Chapter 2 is Mother of Stones (石母) 4. The seventh boss defeated by the player in Chapter 4 is Right-Hand Worm

db_evidence.notes: For 3 of the 4 clue intervals the DB directly resolves the true boss identity and thereby the statement's truth value via literal-name lookups in `entities`/`topic_facts`: (a) 67466-67565s -> real boss is '赤焰麒麟' (Red Flame Qilin), not 'Flint Commander' -> statement 1 false; (b) 28900-29194s -> real boss is '青背龍 (green-backed dragon)', exact match to statement 2's wording, confirmed by a 0.886-score topic_facts hit reading 'on-screen text identifies the boss as 青背龍' -> statement 2 true; (c) 51360-51469s -> real boss is 'boss: 石手蛛 (scorpion/insect-like boss)', not 'Right-Hand Worm' -> statement 4 false. Statement 3 (Mother of Stones/石母 as the 5th chapter-2 boss) could NOT be directly confirmed by any literal name search: '石母' never appears anywhere in entities, episodes, or topic_facts in this DB, so no rollout produced hard textual evidence for it; all 5 rollouts nonetheless accepted statement 3 as true (consistent with the reference answer), apparently by elimination/default rather than positive verification. Chapter boundaries themselves are also noisy: auto-extracted '回' (chapter) title-card entities are inconsistently labeled (e.g. a card at 62820s is captioned 'calligraphic title card 第四回' while a nearby card at 63120s is separately captioned 'chapter 3: 日落红尘'), which undermines any ordinal 'Nth boss in chapter X' count built from these markers.

root_causes: The memory DB's auto-generated entity/episode captions give the same recurring boss many different English/Chinese aliases across nearby 30-second clips, so literal-name lookups are the only reliable verification method, but not all rollouts consistently used them.

The critical reasoning heuristic for this hallucination-detection question type -- 'no literal or near-literal name match anywhere in the DB near the claimed interval implies the claim is fabricated' -- was applied correctly and symmetrically only by rollout-02; the other four rollouts applied it inconsistently, sometimes crediting a claimed boss name as true purely because they could not find positive counter-evidence, and in one case (rollout-04) rejecting the one statement that had the strongest confirming evidence.

Chapter (回) boundary markers extracted into the DB are themselves inconsistently labeled/duplicated, making a robust ordinal 'Nth boss defeated in chapter X' count hard to construct from event_chains/event_steps windows alone; no rollout built a single deduplicated, chapter-scoped, time-ordered boss-defeat list before answering.

No rollout invoked clip_qa to visually confirm a boss's on-screen name text at the ambiguous intervals, even though the question is a name/ordinal check that a single visual sample could resolve cheaply; all reasoning stayed text-only over noisy auto-captions.
what_worked: Rollout-02 ran a single run_sql query against `entities` with all four claimed boss names/aliases (石母, 青背, 右手, 燧) at once, and cross-checked with a second identical sweep over `topic_facts` late in the trace, converging on 'only 青背龍 has any literal match' -- correctly rejecting statements 1 and 4 and accepting statement 2 with hard evidence.

All rollouts correctly located the exact clue-window evidence for statement 2 (青背龍 at 28860-29220s, matching the question's wording almost verbatim); the failures were in how that finding was combined with the other three statements' verdicts, not in retrieval.
transferable_lessons: For 'which statements are hallucinated' questions about a named entity/boss at a given time, run one direct literal-name (and known-alias) search against entities/topic_facts/episodes at the claimed interval; treat a total absence of any matching name there as strong evidence the statement is false, not as inconclusive -- apply this symmetrically across all statements in the question rather than only for some.

Do not let 'I could not find any evidence against this claim' become 'therefore this claim is true' -- for hallucination-detection questions the burden of proof should be on finding positive matching evidence, since these questions are constructed by swapping in plausible-sounding but wrong names.

Before answering an ordinal claim like 'the Nth boss in chapter X', build one deduplicated, time-ordered list of boss-defeat events scoped to that chapter's actual time boundaries (cross-checked against the chapter title-card entity, not an assumed fixed-hour window) rather than issuing several inconsistent ad-hoc windowed queries whose boss-order conclusions differ from rollout to rollout.

When auto-generated chapter/act boundary labels in the DB are inconsistent or duplicated, resolve the ambiguity with a targeted clip_qa call at the title-card timestamp rather than guessing an hour-based cutoff.
open_questions: Whether 'Mother of Stones (石母)' is genuinely the correct name for the boss encountered at 12900-13042s could not be confirmed from this DB (no literal '石母' text anywhere); it is unclear whether the reference answer relies on external game knowledge (Black Myth: Wukong boss lore) not captured by this DB's auto-captions, or whether the true DB evidence for it exists under yet another alias not tried in these searches.

Whether any rollout (or a hypothetical clip_qa call) could have visually read on-screen boss-name text at 12900-13042s or 67466-67565s to confirm/deny the claims more directly was not tested, since no rollout invoked clip_qa for this question.
